title: HTTP and JSON as code: a typed CRM client

concept.heading: A connector is a class: one method per action, typed in and typed out
paragraphs: Every custom connector you have configured is a list of actions with an input schema and an output schema. In code that list is a class. DonorClient has one method per CRM action, and each method returns a pydantic model, not a dict, so a typo in a field name is caught the moment the response is parsed rather than three steps later in a flow.

The second idea is naming failures. The CRM says 404 when a donor does not exist. A dict-returning client would hand back an empty body and let the caller guess. DonorNotFound carries the donor id and a message, so the tool layer you build in Module 1 can turn it into an error the model can act on.

Watch the simulation: the model never touches HTTP. The middleware turns a tool call into a request with headers and a query string, validates the response, and hands back trimmed data. That boundary is where you work for the rest of the track.
concept.lowCodeEquivalent: Copilot Studio's custom connector actions, or the HTTP module in n8n with a Set node that renames fields. The schema you clicked together there is a pydantic class here.

pythonBlock.title: Python you need: classes, type hints, and pydantic models
pythonBlock.intro: A pydantic BaseModel validates data at construction. A class holds the base URL once and reuses it in every method.

spec: Implement DonorClient.find_donors(q), get_donor(id), and get_donations(id) against the mock CRM (shapes in mock_services/crm.py).
Every method returns pydantic models (Donor, Donation), never raw dicts.
A 404 raises DonorNotFound(donor_id); any other non-2xx raises CrmError with the status code in the message.
Keep one httpx.Client per call or per client instance; either is fine, but set the timeout.
askClaudeFor: A review of your error mapping: which status codes become which exception.
How model_validate and a list comprehension turn a JSON array into list[Donation].
writeYourself: The three methods, including the status-code branch in each.
The DonorNotFound raise and the message that names the id.

check.command: uv run --directory middleware python checks/run.py m0-2-http-json
check.summary: Calls your client against a fresh mock CRM: typed donors and donations come back, near-duplicate names stay distinct, and donor 999 raises DonorNotFound.
